message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and the McDonald's All‑American Game MVP.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2007, 2012, 2013, 2020), earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013), and has been selected to the All‑NBA First Team 18 times (as of 2023). He is also a prolific scorer, rebounder, and playmaker, known for his versatility, athleticism, and basketball IQ.

Beyond the court, LeBron is a prominent philanthropist and entrepreneur. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which has donated millions to education and community programs, most notably the “I Promise” school in Akron. He has also produced films and television shows, co‑owned the sports network ESPN+, and launched the media company SpringHill Entertainment.

LeBron James is celebrated not only for his on‑court achievements but also for his leadership, activism, and impact on popular culture.
